Purchases made mainly for family consumption

questions.explanation: Licensing grants rights to use patents, brands or processes.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of marketing. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following terms: (i) needs; (ii) wants; (iii) demand; (iv) exchange. [8 marks]
(c) Explain five functions of marketing. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the process of identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer needs profitably through exchange
2 marks: (b)(i) needs: basic human requirements such as food, clothing and shelter
2 marks: (b)(ii) wants: the particular forms needs take, shaped by culture and personality, e.g. jollof rice
2 marks: (b)(iii) demand: wants backed by ability and willingness to pay
2 marks: (b)(iv) exchange: obtaining a desired product from someone by offering something in return
10 marks: (c) any five, 2 marks each: buying; selling; transportation; storage/warehousing; standardisation and grading; financing; risk bearing; market research; promotion
questions.explanation: Marketing satisfies customer needs profitably. Needs are basic requirements; wants are specific forms; demand is wants backed by purchasing power; exchange is giving something for something. Functions include buying, selling, transport, storage, grading, financing, risk bearing and research.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of a marketing concept. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following concepts: (i) production concept; (ii) product concept; (iii) selling concept; (iv) marketing concept; (v) societal marketing concept. [15 marks]
(c) Which of the concepts in (b) is most suitable for a modern business? Give a reason. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a management philosophy that guides how a firm conducts its marketing activities
3 marks: (b)(i) production: consumers prefer products that are available and cheap, so the firm focuses on efficient mass production
3 marks: (b)(ii) product: consumers prefer products of the best quality and features, so the firm focuses on product improvement
3 marks: (b)(iii) selling: consumers will not buy enough unless persuaded, so the firm emphasises aggressive selling and promotion
3 marks: (b)(iv) marketing: the firm identifies customer needs and satisfies them better than competitors
3 marks: (b)(v) societal marketing: satisfies customer needs and company goals while protecting society's long-term welfare
1 mark: (c) marketing concept or societal marketing concept
2 marks: (c) reason: it focuses on customer satisfaction (and social welfare), leading to loyalty and long-term profit
questions.explanation: A marketing concept is a guiding philosophy. Production focuses on cheap availability; product on quality; selling on aggressive promotion; marketing on customer needs; societal marketing adds society's welfare. The marketing/societal concept suits modern firms because customer focus builds loyalty and long-term profit.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of the marketing mix. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the four elements of the marketing mix. [8 marks]
(c) Explain how each of the following environmental factors may affect a firm's marketing: (i) political; (ii) technological; (iii) cultural; (iv) economic; (v) religious. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the set of controllable marketing variables the firm combines to satisfy its target market
2 marks: (b) product: the goods or services offered, including quality, design and branding
2 marks: (b) price: the amount customers pay, including discounts and credit terms
2 marks: (b) place: distribution channels and outlets that make the product available
2 marks: (b) promotion: advertising, sales promotion, personal selling and publicity
2 marks: (c)(i) political: government policies, laws, bans, taxes
2 marks: (c)(ii) technological: new production methods, online selling, changes in products
2 marks: (c)(iii) cultural: customs and values affecting tastes and acceptance of products
2 marks: (c)(iv) economic: income, inflation and exchange rates affecting purchasing power
2 marks: (c)(v) religious: beliefs that restrict or encourage consumption of certain products
questions.explanation: The marketing mix is product, price, place and promotion. Environmental factors include politics (laws, bans), technology (new methods), culture (tastes), economy (income, inflation) and religion (dietary rules), which firms must adapt to.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of consumer behaviour. [2 marks]
(b) Describe, in logical order, the stages in the consumer buying decision process. [10 marks]
(c) State four factors that influence consumer behaviour. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the way individuals select, buy, use and dispose of goods and services to satisfy their needs
2 marks: (b) need recognition: the consumer becomes aware of a need
2 marks: (b) information search: seeks information from friends, adverts, shops
2 marks: (b) evaluation of alternatives: compares brands, prices and features
2 marks: (b) purchase decision: chooses and buys a product
2 marks: (b) post-purchase behaviour: satisfaction or dissatisfaction, repeat purchase or complaint
8 marks: (c) any four, 2 marks each: cultural; social (family, reference groups); personal (age, income, occupation); psychological (motivation, perception, attitude); price; advertising
questions.explanation: Consumer behaviour is how people choose and use products. Stages: need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, post-purchase behaviour. Influences: cultural, social, personal and psychological factors.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of pricing. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following pricing strategies: (i) haggling; (ii) cost-plus pricing; (iii) demand-based pricing; (iv) competition-based pricing. [8 marks]
(c) A trader buys 40 cartons of noodles at ₦9,500 each and pays ₦20,000 to transport them. She wants a mark-up of 20% on total cost.
(i) Calculate the cost per carton. [3 marks]
(ii) Calculate the selling price per carton. [3 marks]
(d) State two determinants of price. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the process of setting the amount of money customers pay for a product
2 marks: (b)(i) haggling: buyer and seller bargain until a price is agreed
2 marks: (b)(ii) cost-plus: a fixed percentage mark-up is added to the cost
2 marks: (b)(iii) demand-based: price set according to how much customers are willing to pay
2 marks: (b)(iv) competition-based: price set in relation to rivals' prices
3 marks: (c)(i) total cost 40 x 9,500 + 20,000 = ₦400,000; cost per carton ₦10,000
3 marks: (c)(ii) 10,000 + 20% = ₦12,000 per carton
4 marks: (d) any two: cost of production; demand; competition; government regulation; objectives of the firm (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: Pricing sets the amount customers pay. Haggling is bargaining; cost-plus adds a mark-up; demand pricing follows willingness to pay; competition pricing follows rivals. Total cost = 380,000 + 20,000 = 400,000, so ₦10,000 per carton; with 20% mark-up the price is ₦12,000.

questions.stem:
(a) Define advertising. [2 marks]
(b) State four functions of advertising. [8 marks]
(c) State one advantage and one disadvantage of each of the following advertising media: (i) radio; (ii) newspaper; (iii) billboard; (iv) social media. [8 marks]
(d) Suggest a suitable medium for advertising a new brand of yam flour to rural women in Ondo State, giving a reason. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a paid, non-personal presentation of goods, services or ideas by an identified sponsor through mass media
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: informs consumers; persuades them to buy; reminds them; introduces new products; builds brand image; increases sales; counters competition
2 marks: (c)(i) radio: reaches non-literate people/cheap; but no visual image/message is short-lived
2 marks: (c)(ii) newspaper: detailed information and can be kept; but not useful to non-literate people/short life
2 marks: (c)(iii) billboard: seen repeatedly by many passers-by; but limited message/expensive to put up
2 marks: (c)(iv) social media: low cost and targeted, wide reach to youth; but limited reach to people without Internet/negative comments spread fast
2 marks: (d) radio (in the local language), because it reaches rural and non-literate audiences cheaply
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid, non-personal promotion. It informs, persuades, reminds and builds brands. Radio is cheap and reaches non-literates but lacks visuals; newspapers give details but need literacy; billboards are seen repeatedly but carry short messages; social media is cheap and targeted but needs Internet access. Local-language radio suits rural Ondo women.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of merchandising. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following elements of merchandising: (i) packaging; (ii) branding; (iii) labelling. [6 marks]
(c) State four functions of packaging. [8 marks]
(d) State four items of information found on the label of a packaged food product in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) all activities that present goods attractively at the point of sale to encourage buying, including packaging, branding, labelling and display
2 marks: (b)(i) packaging: designing and producing the container or wrapper for a product
2 marks: (b)(ii) branding: giving a product a name, sign or symbol that distinguishes it
2 marks: (b)(iii) labelling: attaching information about the product to its package
8 marks: (c) any four, 2 marks each: protects the product; makes handling and storage easy; attracts customers; carries information; identifies the brand; prevents adulteration
4 marks: (d) any four: brand name; ingredients; net weight/volume; manufacturing and expiry dates; NAFDAC registration number; manufacturer's name and address; directions for use (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Merchandising presents goods attractively at the point of sale. Packaging is the container, branding the identifying name or symbol, labelling the information. Packaging protects, eases handling, attracts and informs. Labels show brand, ingredients, weight, dates, NAFDAC number and manufacturer.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a channel of distribution. [2 marks]
(b) Describe three channels of distribution for consumer goods. [6 marks]
(c) State four factors that influence the choice of a channel of distribution. [8 marks]
(d) State two functions of retailers in the channel. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the route or path through which goods move from the producer to the final consumer
2 marks: (b) producer to consumer (direct)
2 marks: (b) producer to retailer to consumer
2 marks: (b) producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer (or via agents)
8 marks: (c) any four, 2 marks each: nature of the product (perishability, value); size and location of the market; capital of the producer; cost of the channel; competitors' channels; government regulations; level of control desired
4 marks: (d) any two, 2 marks each: sell in small quantities; stock a variety of goods; give credit; provide information to consumers and producers; after-sales service
questions.explanation: A channel of distribution is the route goods take to consumers. Channels: direct; via retailer; via wholesaler and retailer. Choice depends on product nature, market, capital, cost, competition and regulations. Retailers break bulk, offer variety, give credit and pass on information.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of warehousing. [2 marks]
(b) Describe three types of warehouses. [6 marks]
(c) State four functions of warehousing in marketing. [8 marks]
(d) State four activities carried out in a warehouse. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the storage of goods in a building from the time they are produced or imported until they are needed
2 marks: (b) private warehouse: owned by a manufacturer or trader for its own goods
2 marks: (b) public warehouse: owned by an independent firm and rented to the public
2 marks: (b) bonded warehouse: under customs control, storing imported goods until duty is paid
8 marks: (c) any four, 2 marks each: bridges the time gap between production and consumption; protects goods; ensures steady supply; price stability; breaking bulk; allows grading and packaging; enables goods to be used as security for loans
4 marks: (d) any four: receiving; sorting and grading; storing; packing; labelling; dispatching; stock recording (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Warehousing stores goods until needed. Types: private, public, bonded. Functions: time utility, protection, steady supply, price stability, breaking bulk, grading. Activities: receiving, sorting, storing, packing, labelling and dispatching.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of international marketing. [2 marks]
(b) State four reasons why a Nigerian firm may engage in international marketing. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three methods of entering a foreign market. [6 marks]
(d) State two documents used in exporting goods. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the marketing of goods and services across national boundaries
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: to earn foreign exchange; to find larger markets; to use excess capacity; to reduce dependence on the home market; to make more profit; government export incentives
2 marks: (c) exporting: selling goods produced at home to foreign buyers directly or through agents
2 marks: (c) licensing/franchising: allowing a foreign firm to use the brand or process for a fee
2 marks: (c) joint venture or direct investment: partnering with or setting up a firm abroad
4 marks: (d) any two: bill of lading; certificate of origin; commercial invoice; export permit; airway bill; insurance certificate (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: International marketing crosses national borders. Firms export to earn foreign exchange, find larger markets, use spare capacity and gain profit. Entry methods: exporting, licensing/franchising, joint venture or direct investment. Export documents include the bill of lading and certificate of origin.
